newsitem.title: USA: Maine electric users leary of deregulation - study.
newsitem.headline: Maine electric users leary of deregulation - study.

text.p: Maine consumers are leary of efforts to deregulate the electric industry and many would be willing to pay more if there were environmental benefits, according to a survey released Wednesday.

The survey conducted for Maine Public Utilities Commission found only 41 percent of residential users and 50 percent of small business consumers favored deregulation while 54.5 of the residential and 47.3 of the businesses opposed the idea.
The survey found, however, that 67.8 percent of residential customers and 73.9 percent of small business customers felt they would benefit from increased competition between electricity suppliers.
PUC commissioned the randon survey of Maine electric users as part of an effort to draft plan for deregulating the industry.
The proposal will be submitted to Legislature next year.

The study found that residential customers were slightly more concerned about reliability than low rates while small business customers overwhelmingly rated the reliability of the service as their top priority.

Asked if they would be willing to pay 10 percent more for electricity if it could be produced by a "cleaner method," 62.5 percent of the business customers and 72 percent of the residential customers said they would.

Electric deregulation is often likened to the 1980s overhaul of the long-distance phone industry. The survey found 51.6 percent of the residential electric users felt they had benefitted from phone deregulation, but only 47.7 percent had studied which long-distance provider was best suited for their needs. --Boston bureau, 617-367-4106
